To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

age-related decreases in GABA(A)(R) α(1) and β(2) subunit protein and increases in α(3) and β(1) subunits in AI are consistent with a shift toward GABA(A)Rs that have slower desensitization properties and may contribute to the observed age-related decreases in auditory cortical response properties and impaired novelty detection.
age-related decreases in GABA(A)-mediated inhibition in AI are associated with changes in GABAergic receptor expression.

the age-related loss of GABAergic synapses in auditory cortex is associated with changes in GABAergic receptor subunit composition that would alter the magnitude, temporal profile, and efficacy of GABAergic inhibition in auditory cortex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of GABA(A)-receptor (GABA(A)-R) in the aging auditory cortex (AI).
the effects of aging on the brain.
the role of GABA(A)-mediated inhibition in the auditory system and its changes with age.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
age-related GABA(A)Rs changes in AI are heterogeneous and are dependent on the subunit and the cortical layer.
age-related decreases in GABAergic transmission in AI may contribute to age-related declines in AI function.
age-related decreases in GABAergic transmission in AI are likely to underpin observed age-associated changes in AI neuronal function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aging in AI is associated with decreased GABA(A)Rs, increased spontaneous activity, and impaired novelty response.
aging is associated with a decline in the number of GABA(A)(α)(1) and (α)(3) subunits, and an increase in (α)(3), in rat AI.
the GABAergic system in rat auditory cortex shows age-related changes that are likely to impact on the processing of information in the elderly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aging auditory cortex shows a decrease in the expression of GABA receptor subunits, which could contribute to age-related changes in auditory cortical processing.

there are significant age-related changes in the composition and function of GABA(A)-mediated inhibitory synapses that may contribute to changes in neuronal response properties in the aged auditory cortex.
age-related changes in inhibitory neurotransmission in AI are not limited to pre-synaptic GABA release and that GABA(A)Rs are also affected.
